title: Connect with Others to Build Mental Toughness
intro: Mental toughness is essential for every Marine. It supports mission readiness, strengthens resilience, and helps you stay focused in high-stress situations. But here's the truth--mental toughness doesn't grow in isolation. It gets stronger through connection.

sections.heading: Stronger Together
sections.markdown: A solid support system boosts confidence and lowers stress. Social fitness—your ability to connect with others—helps Marines navigate tough times by providing emotional support, accountability, and perspective. Being around others who've been through similar challenges reminds you that you're never alone.

sections.heading: How to Build Social Fitness
sections.markdown:
1. **Join the [Single Marine Program (SMP)](https://www.usmc-mccs.org/smp).**
   SMP brings Marines together through group activities, volunteer opportunities, and leadership development. It's a space to share your story, celebrate success, and get the support you need.
2. **Train with purpose.**
   Take part in [Warrior Athlete Readiness & Resilience (WARR)](https://www.usmc-mccs.org/recreation-fitness) strength and conditioning classes. You'll build mental and physical strength alongside others working toward a common goal.
3. **[Volunteer](https://www.usmc-mccs.org/volunteer).**
   Give back and connect with people who share your values. Volunteering builds confidence, reinforces purpose, and strengthens community bonds.

sections.heading: Real Strength Is Asking for Support
sections.markdown:
Mental toughness isn't about going it alone. It's about knowing when to lean on your community and when to step up for others. Be open to connection, share your experiences, and listen when others need you.

Find your community. Build your strength. Be tougher together.

Visit your installation's Semper Fit or SMP office to get started.
